drivingQuestion: In what case do R' Yehuda and the Rabbis disagree about redeeming oneself or one's son first, and why?
outcomeNote: the dispute is narrowed and its underlying principle identified

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא אֶלָּא חָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים — הוּא קוֹדֵם לִבְנוֹ, מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּמִצְוָה דִּידֵיהּ עֲדִיף. כִּי פְּלִיגִי הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא חָמֵשׁ מְשׁוּעְבָּדוֹת וְחָמֵשׁ בְּנֵי חוֹרִין.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yirmeya says: Everyone concedes» that in a case «where there are only five sela» coins available and one has to redeem both himself and his son, «his» own redemption «takes precedence over» that of «his son,» despite the indication to the contrary from the mishna. «What is the reason?» The reason is «that his own mitzva is preferable» to one he performs on behalf of others. «Where they disagree» is in a case «where there is» both land worth «five» sela coins that is «liened» property that had been previously sold to others «and» land worth «five» sela coins that is «unsold» property.

segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: מִלְוָה הַכְּתוּבָה בַּתּוֹרָה — כִּכְתוּבָה בִּשְׁטָר דָּמְיָא, וְדִידֵיהּ אָזֵיל וְטָרֵיף מִמְּשַׁעְבְּדִי, וּבְהָנֵי חָמֵשׁ בְּנֵי חוֹרִין — פָּרֵיק לֵיהּ לִבְרֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara explains the reasoning behind the dispute: «Rabbi Yehuda maintains» that «a loan that is written in the Torah,» i.e., a financial obligation by Torah law, such as redemption of the firstborn son with five sela coins, is «considered as though it is written in a document,» and it can therefore be collected from liened property, as can any loan recorded in a document. Therefore, the five sela coins that are liened property are available for one’s own redemption but not for that of one’s son, as the sale of the property presumably occurred before the birth of his firstborn. «And» therefore the priest «goes and repossesses» the land worth «five» sela that is «liened» property «for his» own redemption, like any debt written in a document; «and with those five» sela of «unsold» property «he redeems his son.» In this manner, one can fulfill both mitzvot.

segments.he: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: מִלְוָה הַכְּתוּבָה בַּתּוֹרָה — לָאו כִּכְתוּבָה בִּשְׁטָר דָּמְיָא, הִלְכָּךְ מִצְוָה דִּידֵיהּ עָדִיף.
segments.en: «And the Rabbis maintain: A loan that is written in the Torah is not considered as though it is written in a document,» since buyers will not know to guard against repossession if it is not written in a document. Therefore, the five sela coins that are liened property are not available for redemption, and consequently «his own mitzva is preferable.» He accordingly redeems himself with the land that is not liened.
